title: Dynamic Entanglement Distribution for Multi-User and Multi-Protocol Quantum Networking
authors: Rui Wang, Marcus J. Clark, Obada Alia, Sima Bahrani, Djeylan Aktas, Matej Peranić, Mario Stipčević, Martin Lončarić, John Rarity, Siddarth K. Joshi, Dimitra Simeonidou
abstract: Dynamic entanglement distribution is a key requirement for scalable, multi-user and multi-protocol quantum networks. We demonstrate a metropolitan-scale entanglement-based quantum communication network enabled by a quantum reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexer (q-ROADM), which dynamically distributes polarisation-entangled photon pairs from a broadband source to six users over deployed campus and metropolitan fibre. The network supports programmable full-mesh, partial-mesh and sliced sub-network configurations, enabling flexible allocation of entanglement resources according to link condition and service requirement. We demonstrate stable six-user full-mesh operation over more than 150 hours, compare full-mesh and time-shared partial-mesh strategies under different source and detector conditions, and realise quantum network slicing with optional/additional interconnection links. We also show that the same infrastructure can support different quantum protocols by showcasing Secure Inaugural Authentication-Transfer (SIAT) combined with Network flooding over multiple paths to improve the security of onboarding a new user. These results demonstrate a q-ROADM-enabled entanglement distribution architecture as a novel route towards reconfigurable, service-oriented quantum networking over optical fibre infrastructure.
summary: The paper presents an experimental demonstration of a metropolitan-scale quantum network using a q-ROADM to dynamically distribute entanglement among multiple users. It proves the feasibility of flexible, service-oriented networking by supporting full-mesh topologies and complex multi-protocol tasks like secure user onboarding (SIAT). This work advances the practical realization of scalable quantum internet infrastructure over existing optical fiber.
main_problem: The core challenge addressed is achieving scalable, dynamic entanglement distribution necessary for multi-user and multi-protocol quantum networks.
main_result: A quantum reconfigurable optical add-drop multiplexer (q-ROADM) architecture was demonstrated to enable stable, service-oriented entanglement distribution over metropolitan fiber, supporting full-mesh connectivity and complex protocols like SIAT.
method: The authors combine hardware demonstration using a q-ROADM with theoretical analysis of key rates and time complexity for establishing authenticated links.
model_or_system: The system is an entanglement-based quantum communication network built upon deployed metropolitan fiber, utilizing a q-ROADM to dynamically allocate polarization-entangled photon pairs from a broadband source to multiple users (up to six).
key_observables: Secret Key Rate (SKR), Quantum Bit Error Rate (QBER), and total time required for establishing authenticated links (SIAT time).
important_parameters: Source heralding efficiency ($\approx 15\%$ favourable, $\approx 3\%$ challenging), detector jitter ($< 100 	ext{ ps}$ favourable), and security parameters ($\epsilon_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the full link-dependent ratio for authentication can be approximated by the time-tagging contribution, and performance is compared between ideal (favourable) and realistic (challenging) operating conditions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the 6-user network architecture using q-ROADM components. Key plots show the stable SKR of all links over $>150$ hours in full-mesh mode, and time analyses compare total SIAT time for different security levels ($\epsilon_c$) and operational conditions.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for dynamic distribution using a q-ROADM. It then details experimental demonstrations of stable multi-user connectivity (full/partial mesh) and compares key generation rates. Finally, it analyzes the time complexity required to establish secure links using the SIAT protocol across varying link conditions.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the physical implementation challenges of quantum networking by proposing a reconfigurable hardware solution (q-ROADM), which is highly relevant for researchers working on photonic quantum information infrastructure and network protocols.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1: A 6-user entanglement-based quantum communication network architecture enabled by a q-ROADM. A type-0 SPDC broadband polarisation entangled photon source is connected to a q-ROADM via 0.8 km campus fibre between SIL and NSQI, supporting scalable, dynamic entanglement distribution. The 6 user modules are also deployed at NSQI connecting to the q-ROADM via the loop-back of another 0.8 km campus link for user A, B,C,F,G, and Bristol metropolitan fibre looping back from Watershed (user D). At each user, there is a polarisation analysis module, two SNSPDs, a time tagger and a computer to exchange the classical information with other users.

Figure 2: (a) q-ROADM architecture for dynamic entan- glement distribution to multiple users. (B) Wavelength assignment for the six-user full-mesh configuration, where each table entry denotes the channel λi assigned to the corresponding link.
Figure 3: Temporal correlation histogram between Alice and Bob when the network is configured to support only the A–B link, with 10-minute integration time and bin- width of 10 ps.
Figure 4: SKR of all 15 links in the six-user full-mesh quantum network. (a) SKR over ≈7 days; (b) zoomed-in SKR over ≈20 hours.

Figure 5: Comparison between full-mesh and time-shared partial-mesh configurations under different normalised source pump powers. (a) Six-user full-mesh topology. (b,c) Two complementary partial-mesh topologies. (d) Total accumulated secret keys over 40 minutes for the full-mesh configuration, compared with two 20-minute partial-mesh configurations under the favourable network operating condition.
